datasets.title: Satellite detected water extent over Chittagong division, Bangladesh as of 8 August 2021
datasets.description: UNOSAT code: FL20210729BGD This map illustrates satellite-detected surface waters in Chittagong division, Bangladesh as observed from a Sentinel-1 image acquired on 8 August 2021 at 17:55 local time. Within the analyzed area of about 18,700 km2 and, about 873 km2 of lands appear to be flooded. The water extent appears to have increased of about 21 km2 since 30 July 2021. Based on Worldpop population data and the detected surface waters in the analyzed area, the potentially exposed population is mainly located in the district of Cox's Bazar with ~393,240 people, Chittagong with ~358,320 people. This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT). Important note: Flood analysis from radar images may underestimate the presence of standing waters in built-up areas and densely vegetated areas due to backscattering properties of the radar signal.. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/satellite-detected-water-extent-over-chittagong-division-bangladesh-as-of-8-august-2021]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: Sentinel-1 SAR imagery from 8 August 2021 was analyzed by UNOSAT analysts through visual interpretation and multi-temporal comparison with 30 July 2021 imagery to detect surface water extent changes. Detected water polygons (873 km2) were overlaid with WorldPop population data to estimate potentially exposed population in affected districts, producing a post-event flood extent map with exposure assessment.
